scenes.say: Now we build a track in Baku, the fastest street circuit on the calendar.
You close the streets with walls for the whole race weekend, not just one day.
Part of the lap runs along the walls of a twelfth-century fortress, protected by UNESCO.
Between those walls the track is just seven point six metres wide, and the car is almost two metres wide.
Then you hit the seafront and stay flat out for more than two kilometres.
At the end of the straight you're doing over three hundred and fifty, into a ninety-degree corner.
The result: six kilometres and twenty corners. One mistake and you're in the wall.
See every track of the season in 3D on LapRadar.

title: How to build an F1 track in Baku
caption: A 12th-century fortress, 7.6 metres between walls and 2.2 km flat out. Every track in 3D: lapradar.com
